#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Backup destination: either a local/mounted path or a scp-style "host:path".
# Override at call time or via the environment, e.g.:
#   BACKUP_DEST=backup-host:/srv/backups/logs ./backup.sh
# Defaults to a local "backups" directory so the script works out of the box.
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-./backups}"

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote destination, e.g. host:/path/to/dir
        scp -q "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path or mount point
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command: chmod +x backup.sh; ./backup.sh; echo "exit: $?"; ls -la backups; rm -f logs-*.tar.gz; rm -rf backups
